conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have three children - Alex, Blake, and Charlie. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! You have three children: Alex, Blake, and Charlie.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for each of them, I need to gather some more details.

**Let me start by asking: How old are Alex, Blake, and Charlie?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 3, Blake is 8, and Charlie is 10.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! So Alex is 3, Blake is 8, and Charlie is 10 - all under 16 years old, which is good.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with the children:

**Do you live with Alex, Blake, and Charlie?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex and Charlie live with me, but Blake doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. So Alex and Charlie live with you, but Blake doesn't.

For Blake, who doesn't live with you, I need to ask: **Are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards Blake's upkeep - for example on food, clothes, or pocket money?**

(Child Benefit is currently £25.60 per week for the eldest eligible child and £16.95 per week for additional children.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not contributing financially towards Blake's upkeep at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a follow-up question about Blake:

**When did Blake stop living with you? Was it within the last 8 weeks, or longer ago than that?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was longer ago than 8 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Now, just to confirm a few more details about Alex and Charlie who live with you:

**Are Alex and Charlie in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation paid for by the local council?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Blake has been in hospital for a while now - a few months. But I still regularly buy things for him like clothes and magazines and his favorite snacks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that important information about Blake. That changes things.

Let me ask some clarifying questions about Blake's situation:

**How long has Blake been in hospital - approximately how many weeks or months?**

And just to confirm: **You mentioned you regularly buy things for Blake like clothes, magazines, and snacks. Can you estimate roughly how much you spend on Blake per week or per month?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Blake has been in hospital for about 18 weeks now. I'd say I spend around what Child Benefit would be - I keep buying him what he needs while he's there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that clarification. That's very helpful.

So Blake has been in hospital for about 18 weeks (which is more than 12 weeks), but you are regularly spending money on him - approximately what Child Benefit would be worth.

According to the rules, for children in UK hospitals for more than 12 weeks, you can still be entitled to Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on them, which you are doing.

Now, just to complete my assessment, let me confirm about Alex and Charlie:

**Are Alex and Charlie in hospital, in care, or in any residential accommodation? And are there any other circumstances I should know about regarding any of the three children - such as them working, claiming benefits in their own right, or living abroad?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex and Charlie aren't in hospital or care - they're just at home with me. None of the children work or claim any benefits themselves, and we all live here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just confirm one final detail:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, Blake, or Charlie?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for any of them.

**Charlie (age 10):** ✓ Eligible

Since nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for any of your children, you can proceed with claiming for all three of them. Only one person can claim Child Benefit per child, so you'll be the claimant for Alex, Blake, and Charlie.

Do you have any questions about your eligibility or what to do next?
